text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool nb-prod-pool-9 (NewBridge Inc / vpc-374) GPU utilization 96% for 12m, queue_length=182, p95_latency_tokens=240ms. Severity: P1. Paging on-call.

jordan (oncall-sre): acked. I'm pulling metrics and taking pager.

amy (eng-runtime): i'm on graphing now — looks like a single tenant spike from newbridge-prod-rt, sustained token generation workload. No node OOMs, just queueing.

miguel (ops-lead): do we have autoscale enabled on this dedicated pool?

amy (eng-runtime): Not automated for single-tenant enterprise pools unless org approves burst. There's a manual burst override in the control plane.

jordan (oncall-sre): quick customer-impact check: SEAN?

sean (support): NewBridge monitoring shows elevated error rates (429 rate-limited) in their frontend for last 8m. They've opened a ticket but no public outage reported yet.

carla (acct-manager): I'm on the phone with NewBridge's SRE lead — they're seeing user-facing latency for chat experiences. They want mitigation asap and are ok with temporary overage charges.

lee (eng-ml): if we enable burst we can add 2 extra GPUs to pool immediately but we need approval and a duration. Suggest 45 minutes first to stabilize, plus routing to smaller model (gpt-small-quant) for non-critical calls.

jordan (oncall-sre): recommended mitigations: 1) manual burst override +2 gpus for 45m 2) apply rate-limit backpressure on non-priority routes 3) fallback route for non-authenticated sessions -> gpt-small-quant 4) enable prefix caching for repeated prompts. Which do we want to run now?

amy (eng-runtime): I can flip fallback routes and prefix caching in ~2min. Burst override requires ops approval.

miguel (ops-lead): i'm authorizing emergency burst. Activate +2 gpus for 45m. Track cost and CAP alert.

carla (acct-manager): confirmed with NewBridge. authorize burst and temporary routing. I'll tell them ETA ~5m.

jordan (oncall-sre): executing burst override now.

jordan (oncall-sre): ```bash
# manual burst override
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/api/v1/pools/nb-prod-pool-9/burst \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"override":true,"add_gpus":2,"duration_minutes":45,"reason":"customer-impact-NewBridge-P1"}'
```

incident-bot: ACTION: burst_override applied by jordan. +2 gpus scheduled (id=bust-9921), expires in 45m.

amy (eng-runtime): enabling fallback route: route newbridge/* -> gpt-small-quant for non-priority header X-NB-PRIO!=1. Rolling in 3 shards.

jordan (oncall-sre): applying rate-limit to public (non-priority) routes: 30rps per IP.

sean (support): confirming NewBridge is seeing improvement on first tests. They report p95 down from 6s -> 1.2s for critical flows.

lee (eng-ml): queue_length dropped from 182 -> 22 after burst + routing. GPU util now 68% on pool nodes.

miguel (ops-lead): nice. Keep burst for now. We need to triage root cause — sustained customer load pattern wasn't covered by existing autoscale policy.

carla (acct-manager): NewBridge wants a short post-incident note and will request a follow-up call to discuss committed burst or increased reserved capacity. I'll schedule.

jordan (oncall-sre): I'm leaving a short incident note in the runbook: "nb-prod-pool-9: manual burst activated 2 GPUs for 45m at 3250005562 due to tenant spike. Fallback route and caching enabled."

amy (eng-runtime): logging commands we ran to rollback later:
```bash
# remove fallback
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/api/v1/pools/nb-prod-pool-9/routes/rollback -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -d '{"route":"newbridge/*"}'
```

jordan (oncall-sre): note: if burst expires and load remains high we will coordinate with Miguel for extension or advise customer on committed capacity.

miguel (ops-lead): agreed. Also action item: add autoscale policy rule for single-tenant pools that can pre-authorize up to +2 GPUs with billing cap and auto-notify account team.

lee (eng-ml): action: evaluate model quantization for NewBridge workloads — could reduce token compute by ~30%. I'll run evals.

sean (support): I've logged the customer-facing update in the ticket: "We've applied a temporary capacity increase and routing changes; engineering monitoring shows improvements. We'll follow up with a detailed post-incident package."

carla (acct-manager): scheduling follow-up meeting with NewBridge for tomorrow 10am PT.

jordan (oncall-sre): monitoring window open. I'll stay on pager for next 30m.

incident-bot: UPDATE: burst_override id=bust-9921 active; current_gpu_count=4; pool_util=66%; queue_length=18. Next automated check in 5m.

amy (eng-runtime): after 12m of observation, metrics remain stable. I'll prepare a short incident summary draft.

miguel (ops-lead): once burst expires, plan: 1) auto-evaluate extension if queue_length>50 2) if repeated spikes, offer NewBridge committed + reserved capacity or autoscale policy change.

jordan (oncall-sre): closing active pager but keeping incident channel live for postmortem notes.

carla (acct-manager): thanks team — customer relays appreciation.

lee (eng-ml): note to self: add a workload profile for NewBridge to model-catalog and flag candidate quantized variants.

jordan (oncall-sre): INCIDENT CLOSED -> will file post-incident report and link to this thread.

sean (support): ticket updated and customer notified.

amy (eng-runtime): post-incident actions: (1) add autoscale pre-approval flow for enterprise pools, (2) add detection rule to notify account-team earlier, (3) review default routing fallbacks.

miguel (ops-lead): assigning follow-ups in tracker.

incident-bot: RESOLVE: incident id=inc-3250005555 resolved at 3250005678.
